AGENDA

PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA 90274
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
CALL TO ORDER

Due to State law, no action can be taken by the Council this evening on matters presented under this section. If the Council determines action is warranted, the item may be referred to staff or placed on a future Council agenda.
CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1-10)
All items under this heading are considered to be routine and will be enacted by one motion, unless a Councilmember or staff requests that an item be removed for separate discussion. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered immediately following the motion to approve the Consent Agenda.

Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the minutes for the following special meetings: September 5, 2024 and September 10, 2024.

Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the minutes for the Planning Commission meeting of October 15, 2024.

CONSIDER AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE AGREEMENT WITH BENNETT LANDSCAPING TO MODIFY THE ANNUAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF $1,506,746 TO $1,386,406 FOR YEAR 1; APPROVE A ONE-YEAR EXTENSION FOR CITYWIDE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,386,406 FOR YEAR 2; AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER THE OPTION TO EXTEND THE CONTRACT FOR AN ADDITIONAL TWO, ONE-YEAR EXTENSIONS SUBJECT TO CPI ADJUSTMENTS STARTING YEAR 4; AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AMENDMENT NO.2.
Recommendation: Staff recommends That the City Council:
1.
Consider Amendment No. 2 to the Agreement with Bennett Landscaping (Bennett) to modify the annual not to exceed amount of $1,506,746 to $1,386,406 for Year 1;
2.
Approve a one-year extension for Citywide Landscape Maintenance in the amount of $1,386,406 for Year 2;
3.
Authorize the City Manager the option to extend the contract for an additional two, one-year extensions subject to Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustments starting Year 4; and
4.
Authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 2.

6.
CONSIDER A NEW MUNICIPAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL FOR FISCAL YEARS 2024-2029

8.
CONSIDER AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MNS TO CONTINUE TO PROVIDE AN ASSSITANT PLANNER LEVEL PROFESSIONAL CONTRACT PLANNING SERVICES ASSISTANT PLANNER
Recommendation: It is recommended by the City Council to approve Amendment #2 to the Professional Services Agreement with MNS for $30,000 to fund professional contract planning services Assistant Planner level through February 28, 2025 (4 months) and authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment #2.
Staff Report
9.
CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL OF THE PUBLIC AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025
Recommendation: It is recommended by the City Council approve the Public Available Pay Schedule for fiscal year 2024-2025.
Staff Report
Revised Staff Report
10.
ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION R24-52 REGARDING THE APPOINTMENT OF AN INTERIM PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR
Recommendation: That the City Council Approve Resolution No. R24-52 appointing Philip Lanzafame as Interim Public Works Director.
Staff Report
OLD BUSINESS
11.
MALAGA LANE WATER INTRUSION AND SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION
Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council receive an update on the Malaga Lane water intrusion and subsurface investigation and provide directions to staff.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 22, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES

CALL TO ORDER AT 6:30 P.M.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ROLL CALL
PRESENT: Mayor Murdock, Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi, Council Member Kemps, Council
  Member McGowan

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Kallman, City Attorney Rusin, City Clerk Cook, Community
  Development Director Brady, City Engineer Loriso, Chief Hellinga, and City
  Treasurer Greenberg

APPROVAL OF AGENDA
ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Murdock and Seconded by Council Member Kemps to move
  the ceremonial presentations ahead of the Mayor’s report and approve the
  agenda.

AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
NOES: None

CEREMONIAL PRESENTATIONS

LIFE SAVING AWARD – Chief Hellinga presented life savings awards to Acting Sergeant
Sean Crisfield, Officer Neil Sisson, Firefighter Paramedics Derrick Ho, Frank Guitierrez, and
Alan Matsumoto, and PVPUSD Registered Nurse Ralista “Railli” Berkovski-Varbanov

PROCLAMATION: Honoring Eleazar “Alic” Abrego Upon His Retirement – Mayor Murdock
read a proclamation thanking Alic for his 43 years of service. City Manager Kallman and
Anthony Mendoza provided comments regarding Alic’s works and thanked him for his service
and awarded him with a custom shirt and street sign.

MAYOR’S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Mayor Murdock announced Council Member Roos’ resignation due to a move to Austin Texas
and stated council will not be filling the seat as a new council will be in place in December.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
 She thanked him for his service and sense of humor. The Mayor shared she attended the
Friday night homecoming game at PVHS and thanked residents for their patience and
understanding while putting up with the accompanying inconveniences that come with the
annual homecoming activities. She reminded the public of the upcoming joint meeting with
the Planning Commission on October 30, 2024 to discuss the draft comprehensive objective
design standards, that the Lunada Bay Harvest Festival is October 27 from 2-6 P.M., and to
vote on November 5.

In her “Did You Know” segment, Mayor Murdock noted seeing houses placing trash cans at
the curb. She reminded residents that PVE Municipal Codes 8.16.020 and 8.16.090 state
trash cans need to be concealed and on private property and doing otherwise is a code
violation.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Kallman reminded residents of Sunday’s Prepared Peninsula Expo at Peninsula
High School from 10 A.M. to 1 P.M. He thanked Anthony Mendoza and John Strum for their
after-hours service to address fallen trees.

City Clerk Cook provided information related to the upcoming election and the various
locations and hours of operation to vote in person and submit mail-in ballots.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC
Council was addressed by Christine Fine, Phyllis Scribe, Valerie Gorsuch, John Weick, Parvin
Jensen, Darcel Rameriz-Hanson, and Terry Pearson.

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1-10)
Items #1, 5, 8, and 10 were pulled.
There was no public comment.

ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi and Seconded by Council Member Kemps to
  approve the consent agenda items 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and 9.

AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
NOES: None

2.  RECEIVE AND FILE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE PERIOD ENDING
  SEPTMEBER 30, 2024

  Received and Filed the financial statements for the month ending September 30,
  2024.

3.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS

  Approved the minutes for the following special meetings: September 5, 2024 and
  October 8, 2024.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
 4.  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING ACTIONS

  Received and Filed minutes for the Planning Commission meeting of October 15,
  2024.

6.  CONSIDER A NEW MUNICIPAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL FOR FISCAL YEARS
  2024-2029

  Approved the contract and authorized the City Manager and City Attorney to
  execute the agreement between the Los Angeles County Department of Animal
  Care and Control (DACC).

 7. CONSIDERATION OF A LETTER OF SUPPORT TO LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA
  CITIES REGARDING A GENERAL ASSEMBLY RESOLUTION

  Authorized the Mayor to sign this letter of support on behalf of the City Council of
  the city of Palos Verdes Estates.

9.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL OF THE PUBLIC AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE
  FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025

  Approved the Public Available Pay Schedule for fiscal year 2024-2025.

  Items Pulled from Consent

1.  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS
  City Treasurer announced a check for So Cal Gas needed to be added to the warrants.

  There was no public comment.

  ACTION: Moved by Council Member McGowan and Seconded by Council Member
  Kemps to approve the warrants as amended.

  AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES: None

5.  CONSIDER AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE AGREEMENT WITH BENNETT
  LANDSCAPING TO MODIFY THE ANNUAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF
  $1,506,746 TO $1,386,406 FOR YEAR 1; APPROVE A ONE-YEAR EXTENSION FOR
  CITYWIDE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,386,406 FOR
  YEAR 2; AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER THE OPTION TO EXTEND THE
  CONTRACT FOR AN ADDITIONAL TWO, ONE-YEAR EXTENSIONS SUBJECT TO
  CPI ADJUSTMENTS STARTING YEAR 4; AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER
  TO EXECUTE AMENDMENT NO.2.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
   Mayor Murdock expressed concerns that the six issues she brought up at the October
  8 discussion on this item were not addressed. Council asked additional clarifying
  questions. Staff and Sean Bennett of Bennett Landscaping responded.

  Council expressed the need to provide more information to the public regarding the
  use of herbicides to both educate and inform. Information needs to be on the city
  website and bi-weekly updates and include information on when and where herbicides
  will be used and a set of FAQs to address residents’ concerns including the safety of
  products. Council also directed Staff to provide an annual presentation on how the
  contract is doing relative to our goals.

  Council was addressed by Darcel Ramirez-Hanson.

  ACTION: Moved by Council Member McGowan and Seconded by Council Member
  Kemps to approve the contract as staff has proposed, that staff, on an annual
  basis, review the progress against our milestones and goals of the contract
  including the use of pesticides, and that the City Manager find ways to
  communicate these pertinent facts to our residents.

  AYES: Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES: Murdock

8.  CONSIDER AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH MNS TO CONTINUE TO PROVIDE AN ASSSITANT PLANNER
  LEVEL PROFESSIONAL CONTRACT PLANNING SERVICES ASSISTANT PLANNER

  Council asked clarifying questions. regarding timing and likely success of hiring a
  planner.

  There was no public comment.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi and Seconded by Council Member
  McGowan to approve Amendment No. 2 to the professional services
  agreement with MNS for $30,000 to fund professional contract planning
  services at the Assistant Planner level through February 2025 and authorize
  the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 2.

  AYES: Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES: Murdock

10.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION R24-52 REGARDING THE APPOINTMENT OF AN
  INTERIM PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR
  City Attorney Rusin announced that changes were made to the resolution and draft
  agreement to be CalPERS compliant. Council asked clarifying questions.

  There was no public comment.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
   ACTION: Moved by Council Member Kemps and Seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi
  to approve Resolution R24-52 as amended appointing Phillip Lanzafame as
  Interim Public Works Director.

  AYES: Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES: Murdock

OLD BUSINESS
11. MALAGA LANE WATER INTRUSION AND SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION.
  City Engineer Loriso provided a staff report. He reported that the sink hole and voids in
  Malaga Lane have been filled with slurry at a cost within the amount approved by
  Council. Council asked clarifying questions. City Manager Kallman provided an update
  regarding the Steering Committee meetings and options Staff is investigating. Council
  expressed a desire to ensure all affected property owners are aware of the City’s efforts.
  It was suggested a post card be sent to all owners informing them Council is discussing
  the water issues at every council meeting. Staff reported the next Geosyntec study
  should be available in a month. Council expressed a desire for staff to see if the report
  can be expedited since council is dark in December and they would prefer not to wait
  until January.

  Council was addressed by Scott Rosenberg.

MAYOR AND COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS & TENTATIVE FUTURE AGENDA

Council discussed the tentative agenda items. Council Member McGowan shared the PVE
Foundation would like to provide a presentation on the ALPR cameras. City Manager Kallman,
shared Staff is planning to update the ADU ordinance by January 1.

ADJOURNMENT TO TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 12, 2024, AT 6:30 P.M.
Meeting was adjourned at 8:43 P.M.

Respectfully submitted:

________________________________
Tameka Cook, City Clerk

  APPROVED:

  _______________________________
  Dawn Murdock, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
